name: Montana veterans: Veterans Affairs Division service officers for claims help
organization: Montana Department of Military Affairs, Veterans Affairs Division (MVAD)
description: Free help from MVAD’s accredited Veteran Service Officers: VA compensation and pension claims, appeals and hearings, survivor claims, military records and referrals, from nine offices and outreach visits across Montana.
next_step: Call the nearest office (choose a county above) or the division at 406-324-3742.
constraints: Service officers travel for outreach; call ahead for times and places.

source_evidence.title: Montana Veterans Affairs Division: Veteran Services
source_evidence.scope: Nine Veteran Service Offices with phones and emails, the division line 406-324-3742 and address, and what service officers do; read in full.

name: Montana Area Agencies on Aging and Aging and Disability Resource Centers
organization: Montana DPHHS Office on Aging and the Area Agencies on Aging
description: Montana’s Area Agencies on Aging, most also Aging and Disability Resource Centers, give information, options counseling and help with in-home services, meals, caregiver support and benefits. One toll-free line rings the local agency. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 1-800-551-3191, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

source_evidence.scope: Each ADRC with phone and counties served; read in full.

name: Medicare counseling (Montana SHIP)
organization: Montana DPHHS Office on Aging, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), through the Area Agencies on Aging
description: Free, confidential health-benefits counseling for Medicare beneficiaries and their families from SHIP counselors at the Area Agencies on Aging.
next_step: Call 1-800-551-3191; staff refer you to the SHIP counselor at your county’s Area Agency on Aging. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

source_evidence.title: Montana DPHHS: State Health Insurance Assistance Program
source_evidence.scope: No-cost Medicare counseling; call 1-800-551-3191 to be referred to the local Area Agency on Aging’s SHIP counselor; search excerpt.

name: Montana Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Montana DPHHS: Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other long-term care settings, through regional ombudsmen and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of people 60 and older and adults with disabilities.
next_step: Choose a county above for its ombudsman, or call the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 406-444-3285. To report abuse, call Adult Protective Services at 1-844-277-9300 (weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.) or report online any time at aps.mt.gov. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

source_evidence.scope: Regional and state ombudsman phones and counties; read in full.

name: Free legal help for older Montanans
organization: Montana Legal Services Association; DPHHS Office on Aging, Legal Services Developer
description: Montana Legal Services Association gives free civil legal help to people with low incomes statewide. The Legal Services Developer in the state Office on Aging provides elder law resources, legal referrals and basic help with legal documents.
next_step: Apply online at mtlsa.org or call the MLSA HelpLine at 1-800-666-6899 (Tuesday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.). For elder law help, call the Office on Aging’s Legal Services Developer at 800-332-2272.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type; HelpLine hours are limited, so keep trying or apply online.

source_evidence.title: MontanaLawHelp.org: Apply for legal services
source_evidence.scope: HelpLine 1-800-666-6899, Tuesday to Thursday 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.; search excerpt.

source_evidence.title: Montana State Library: Where to find legal information in Montana
source_evidence.scope: Montana Legal Services Developer in the Office on Aging, 800-332-2272: elder law resources, legal referrals and basic help with documents; search excerpt.

name: VA health care in Montana
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Montana Health Care System
description: Montana veterans are served by the VA Montana Health Care System: the Fort Harrison VA Medical Center (3687 Veterans Drive, Fort Harrison; 406-442-6410, toll-free 877-468-8387) and clinics across the state.
next_step: Call 877-468-8387 or 406-442-6410 for appointments. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Veteran Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

source_evidence.title: VA Montana health care: Contact us
source_evidence.scope: Montana VA Medical Center, 3687 Veterans Drive, Fort Harrison; local 406-442-6410, toll-free 877-468-8387; search excerpt.

name: Living Independently for Today and Tomorrow (LIFTT)
organization: Living Independently for Today and Tomorrow
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.

name: Volunteers of America, Northern Rockies: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 20-ZZ-113): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 515-669-1780.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
